content_units: Best Laptop Pick for Your Priorities

For   battery, keyboard comfort, and overall value  , the best fit is   A) Lenovo IdeaPad 5  . It gives you the strongest price-to-performance balance for coding, enough power for light video editing, and a typically comfortable typing experience at the lowest price.
Laptop Value Comparison
Model   Price   CPU   RAM/Storage   Weight   Battery Claim   Best For
Lenovo IdeaPad 5     $799     Ryzen 7 7730U   16GB / 512GB   1.46kg   11 hrs     Best overall value
ASUS Zenbook 14   $999   Core Ultra 5   16GB / 512GB   1.28kg     13 hrs     Best battery + premium feel
Acer Swift Go 14   $899   Core i7-1355U   16GB /   1TB       1.25kg     9 hrs   Best storage + portability
Why the Lenovo IdeaPad 5 wins
-   Best value  : It is $200 cheaper than the Zenbook and $100 cheaper than the Swift Go while still giving you   16GB RAM  , which is the key baseline for CS work.
-   Strong coding machine  : The Ryzen 7 7730U is more than enough for IDEs, many browser tabs, Docker/light VMs, Python, Java, and web development.
-   Usually good keyboard comfort  : IdeaPads are generally known for practical, comfortable keyboards, which matters a lot for long coding sessions.
-   Battery is still solid  : Claimed 11 hours is competitive, and in real use it should be good enough for class and library work.
When the ASUS Zenbook 14 is worth paying more
- Choose this if   battery life is your absolute top priority   and you also want a lighter, more premium machine.
- The   Core Ultra 5   is efficient, and the   13-hour claim   is the best here.
- The   OLED display   is excellent for media and visual work, including light editing.
- Trade-off: you are paying   $200 more than Lenovo   without getting more RAM or storage.
Where the Acer Swift Go 14 stands
- Best if you want   1TB storage   out of the box for projects, footage, and files.
- It is also the   lightest   by a small margin.
- But for your priorities, the   9-hour battery claim   is the weakest of the three.
- Keyboard quality on Swift models is usually decent, but not as consistently praised as Lenovo’s more typing-focused designs.
Final Ranking for a CS Student
1) Lenovo IdeaPad 5 — Best overall value
- Best balance of price, performance, keyboard comfort, and battery
- Smartest buy if you want the most laptop per dollar
2) ASUS Zenbook 14 — Best premium choice
- Best if battery life and portability matter more than price
- Better display, likely better efficiency, but worse value
3) Acer Swift Go 14 — Best if storage matters most
- Good all-rounder, but weaker battery makes it less aligned with your priorities
Buying Context

Using only the specs you gave, I’m weighting your priorities in this order:   battery first, keyboard comfort second, value third  . Since keyboard feel is partly model-line dependent and not fully captured by specs, the recommendation leans on each brand line’s usual reputation as well as the listed hardware.
